articles.title_en: VNIIAES introduced the latest predictive analytics system at the first two power units of Leningrad NPP-2
articles.excerpt: На энергоблоках №1 и №2 Ленинградской АЭС-2 внедрена система предиктивной аналитики оборудования атомной станции, позволяющая увидеть потенциальную проблему в работе оборудования ещё до её…
bullets: На энергоблоках №1 и №2 Ленинградской АЭС-2 внедрена система предиктивной аналитики оборудования атомной станции, позволяющая увидеть потенциальную проблему в работе оборудования ещё до её возникновения.
Проект стартовал ранее на энергоблоке №1 Нововоронежской АЭС-2, а впоследствии был распространён на энергоблок №2 НВАЭС-2, №1 и №2 Ленинградской АЭС-2 и №4 Белоярской АЭС.
Он направлен на повышение эксплуатационной надёжности оборудования АЭС, как одного из ключевых приоритетов в подходах к безопасности в госкорпорации «Росатом».
В рамках программы тиражирования успешного опыта Концерна «Росэнергоатом» новейшие предиктивные модели внедряются и на энергоблоках №1 и №2 Ленинградской АЭС-2.
bullets_en: At the power units No. 1 and No. 2 of the Leningrad NPP-2, a system of predictive analytics of the equipment of the nuclear power plant has been introduced, which allows you to see a potential problem in the operation of the equipment even before it occurs.
The project started earlier at Unit 1 of the Novovoronezh NPP-2, and was subsequently extended to Unit 2 of the NVAES-2, No. 1 and No. 2 of the Leningrad NPP-2 and No. 4 of the Beloyarsk NPP.
It is aimed at improving the operational reliability of NPP equipment as one of the key priorities in approaches to safety at Rosatom.
As part of the program of replicating the successful experience of the Rosenergoatom Concern, the latest predictive models are being introduced at power units No. 1 and No. 2 of the Leningrad NPP-2.

The reactors entered commercial operation in December 2018 and September 2019, respectively.

articles.title_en: Westinghouse to qualify BWXT for AP1000 component manufacture

bullets: Qualification will allow Westinghouse and BWXT to collaborate to enable the manufacturing of large-scale, nuclear-grade components in Canada and the USA for AP1000 projects globally, the companies said.

"By combining BWXT Canada's capabilities with Westinghouse's AP1000 technology and global experience, we are creating new opportunities for Canadian industry to support nuclear projects at home and around the world."
Six AP1000 reactors are in operation in the USA and China and 14 are under construction in China.

articles.title: Start-up milestones for Indian plants
articles.title_en: Start-up milestones for Indian plants
articles.excerpt: As Kaiga unit 1 restarts after a record-breaking refurbishment outage, India's nuclear regulator has given Nuclear Power Corporation of India permission for the First Approach to Criticality for unit 8 at the Rajasthan Atomic Power Project.
bullets: The Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB) said it had granted permission for the First Approach to Criticality for the 700 MWe pressurised water reactor, also known as RAPP unit 8, on 19 November "following satisfactory completion of the requisite safety reviews".

RAPP 8 is the second of two Indian-designed 700 MWe pressurised heavy water reactors (PHWRs) built as a pair at the Rajasthan Atomic Power Project, and the fourth in a series of sixteen such units being set up in the country.
RAPP unit 7 reached full power earlier this year after reaching first criticality in September 2024 and being connected to the grid in March 2025.
The 200 MWe unit, which was first connected to the grid in 2000, "successfully attained criticality early morning of 22nd November 2026", NPCIL said.

articles.title: New York unveils advanced nuclear master plan
articles.title_en: New York unveils advanced nuclear master plan
articles.excerpt: Governor Kathy Hochul has announced the completion of the Master Plan for Responsible Advanced Nuclear Development in New York, which sets out a roadmap for the state to achieve its target of creating 5 GW of new nuclear power capacity.
bullets: The plan, which was co-authored by the New York State Energy Research Development Authority and the New York State Department of Public Service outlines coordinated state actions to support the safe and timely development and deployment of advanced nuclear power plants in upstate New York.
The master plan was developed in response to Hochul’s 2025 directive to establish a framework supporting advanced nuclear energy development in New York.
This is in addition to the 3.4 GWe of nuclear capacity already in existence in the state.

The 30-point Master Plan, which is supported by 12 studies and more than 1,000 pages of research and analysis, identifies New York State actions to further assist with responsible advanced nuclear development.

articles.title: Fuel plates milestone for FRM-II conversion
articles.title_en: Fuel plates milestone for FRM-II conversion
articles.excerpt: Framatome's fabrication of the first depleted uranium fuel plates is a major technical milestone towards the conversion of the FRM II research reactor at Technical University of Munich from highly enriched uranium to high-assay low-enriched uranium fuel.
bullets: The 20 MWt FRM II, operating since 2005, is one of the most effective and modern sources of high-flux neutrons in the world.
However, to generate its dense neutron flux the reactor currently uses highly enriched uranium (HEU) fuel which contains over 95% uranium-235 - and this is seen as a nuclear proliferation risk.
TUM has been collaborating with Framatome since 2019 on a programme to convert the reactor to run on fuel with lower uranium enrichment.

In 2023, the company completed the development of the main component of the innovative monolithic U-Mo fuel, which, thanks to its high uranium density, can enable the reactor to perform as intended while using an enrichment of less than 20% uranium-235 (see Background section below).

bullets: В Норвегии накоплено около 16,5 тонн отработавшего ядерного топлива, образовавшегося за шесть десятилетий эксплуатации исследовательских ядерных реакторов.
Согласно соглашению, действующему до 2055 года, компания Studsvik будет транспортировать топливо на свои лицензированные объекты в Студсвике (недалеко от города Нючёпинг, Швеция).

Минимальная стоимость контракта оценивается примерно в 875 млн шведских крон (88,3 млн долларов США) — при условии, что все топливо будет вывезено в Швецию к 2035 году, — а общая оценочная стоимость работ для компании Studsvik составляет 3–4 млрд шведских крон.

Агентство NND, созданное в 2018 году в качестве государственного органа при Министерстве торговли, промышленности и рыболовства, отвечает за вывод из эксплуатации исследовательских реакторов и другой связанной с ними ядерной инфраструктуры.
bullets_en: Norway has accumulated about 16.5 tons of spent nuclear fuel from six decades of research nuclear reactors.
Under the agreement, which runs until 2055, Studsvik will transport the fuel to its licensed facilities in Studsvik, near Nücöping, Sweden.

The minimum contract value is estimated at approximately SEK 875 million (US$88.3 million) – assuming all fuel is shipped to Sweden by 2035 – and the total estimated value for Studsvik is SEK 3-4 billion.
Established in 2018 as a government agency under the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Fisheries, NND is responsible for decommissioning research reactors and other related nuclear infrastructure.
articles.excerpt_en: Norwegian Nuclear Decommissioning has signed an agreement with Swedish nuclear engineering company Studsvik to handle spent nuclear fuel.

bullets_en: Westinghouse Electric Company plans to start operating the new facility in 2030.

World Energy Outlook

"In an echo of the 1970s, the 2026 crisis is set to reinforce the comeback of nuclear power," the IEA says.

It notes that, as of mid-year, nearly 90 GW of new nuclear capacity was under construction - the highest level for more than 35 years, and more than 50 countries now have plans or targets for nuclear power, including new technologies such as small modular reactors.

articles.title: Hot and cold testing under way for Turkey's Akkuyu 1
articles.title_en: Hot and cold testing under way for Turkey's Akkuyu 1
articles.excerpt: The first nuclear power reactor in Turkey has moved a step closer to start-up, with hot and cold commissioning tests taking place.
bullets: Akkuyu Nuclear Power Plant's unit 1 will have all its equipment in the primary and secondary circuits tested under operating conditions - with checks of equipment strength, piping, vibration, safety systems, reactor control and protection systems.

The commissioning programme involves "gradually warming up the reactor unit and increasing the temperature and pressure of the primary coolant (desalinated water) to their rated values of 285°C and 16.5 MPa.
This pressure is comparable to that experienced by objects submerged at a depth of 1,650 metres and keeps the water in a liquid state", Akkuyu Nuclear JSC explained.
When the 4,800 MWe plant is completed, it is expected to meet about 10% of Turkey's electricity needs.

articles.title: World Nuclear Association Director General Comments on IEA World Energy Outlook 2026
articles.title_en: World Nuclear Association Director General Comments on IEA World Energy Outlook 2026
bullets: The current energy crisis is reinforcing the comeback of nuclear power, with nuclear and renewables emerging as major beneficiaries of the shift towards domestic energy sources, the International Energy Agency’s (IEA) World Energy Outlook 2026 finds.

The report, in line with the World Nuclear Outlook Report , notes that nearly 90 GW of new nuclear capacity was under construction as of mid-2026, the highest level in more than 35 years, and that over 50 countries now have plans or targets for nuclear power.

The IEA has revised its nuclear generation projections upwards compared with last year’s outlook, led by China and the United States, and now sees the prospect of nuclear power growing faster than electricity demand, increasing its share of the electricity mix from the current 9%.

Dr Sama Bilbao y León, Director General, World Nuclear Association, commented, “We welcome the IEA World Energy Outlook 2026 and its clear recognition of the essential role of nuclear energy in the global energy system.

articles.title: IAEA Team Welcomes Ageing Management Improvements At Japan’s Mihama-3
articles.title_en: IAEA Team Welcomes Ageing Management Improvements At Japan’s Mihama-3
articles.excerpt:
An International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) team has welcomed improvements in ageing management at the Mihama-3 nuclear plant in Japan, but said the operator should ensure the adequate coordination and oversight of key activities.

The team, which reviewed the long-term operational safety of Mihama-3, said Kansai Electric Power Company (Kepco) should also ensure the adequate analysis and use of external operating experience from external organisations in the area of long-term operation and improve the analysis and management of data for ageing management.
bullets: Team leader and IAEA nuclear safety officer Martin Marchena said Kepco has made improvements in ageing management and resolved many of the findings identified in an earlier mission 2024.
Mihama-3 is a 780 MW pressurised water reactor unit that began commercial operation in 1973.
It underwent an extended shutdown of approximately 10 years after the Fukushima-Daiichi nuclear power station accident in March 2011.
In 2015, Kepco applied to extend the operational period of Unit 3 from 40 to 60 years until November 2036.

articles.title: World Nuclear Association calls on decision-makers to adopt a risk-informed approach to very low radiation doses
articles.title_en: World Nuclear Association calls on decision-makers to adopt a risk-informed approach to very low radiation doses
bullets: The call comes in a new position statement, Decision-Making at Very Low Doses , developed by the Association’s Radiological Protection Working Group (RPWG), which sets out five practical recommendations to support nuclear energy’s expansion to meet the global energy challenge.

Kari Toews , Director Occupational Safety & Senior Health Physicist at Cameco Corporation, and Chair of the RPWG said: “Radiological protection has served society well, and our industry is fully committed to maintaining the highest standards.
Yet radiation from human activities is regulated however small the dose, even though clear evidence of health risk exists only above about 100 mSv whether received in one instance or over a lifetime.
Everyday comparisons: A chest X-ray gives a dose of about 0.014 mSv, and an intercontinental flight such as London to New York about 0.08 mSv, from cosmic radiation at altitude.

bullets: World Nuclear Association Director General Dr Sama Bilbao y León participated in the International Ministerial Conference on Nuclear Power in the Republic of Korea on 28 October, bringing the nuclear industry’s perspective to high-level discussions on the safe and effective expansion of nuclear energy.

The conference brings together ministers, policymakers and international experts to explore how nuclear power can meet growing energy demand, strengthen energy security and support climate goals and sustainable development.

articles.title: EIB backs Finnish nuclear-technology company Steady Energy with €40 million financing
articles.title_en: EIB backs Finnish nuclear-technology company Steady Energy with €40 million financing
articles.excerpt: Press release · European Commission, SMR policy page
bullets: EIB makes its first investment in small modular reactor (SMR) technology, providing up to €40 million to Finland-based startup Steady Energy.

The European Investment Bank (EIB) is investing up to €40 million in Finnish nuclear-technology company Steady Energy as part of a broader financing package involving institutional, strategic and retail investors.

This is the EIB’s first investment in SMR technology, and supports the European Commission’s strategy to bring Europe’s first Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) and Advanced Modular Reactors (AMRs) online by the early 2030s.
Steady Energy’s 50 MW reactor concept is designed to supply low-carbon heat to district heating networks.

articles.title: Ohi units cleared for another 10 years' operation
articles.title_en: Ohi units cleared for another 10 years' operation
bullets: Under regulations which came into force in July 2013, Japanese reactors had a nominal operating period of 40 years.

One extension to this - limited to a maximum of 20 years - could be granted, requiring amongst other things, a special inspection to verify the integrity of reactor pressure vessels and containment vessels after 35 years of operation.
However, in December 2022, the NRA approved a draft of a new rule that would allow reactors to be operated for more than the current limit of 60 years.

Under the amendment, the operators of reactors in use for 30 years or longer must formulate a long-term reactor management plan and gain approval from the regulator at least once every 10 years if they are to continue to operate.
